label: Telegram
terms_note: BOT accounts only (Bot API 10.3, 24 Aug 2026): https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/METHOD; getUpdates (offset / limit / timeout / allowed_updates) XOR setWebhook (secret_token 1-256 chars, max_connections 1-100 default 40, drop_pending_updates). Bots cannot see other bots' messages; privacy mode in groups hides non-command messages unless the bot is admin / privacy off. Limits (FAQ): ≤1 message per second per chat, ≤20 messages per minute in a group, ≈30 messages per second overall for bulk notifications (paid broadcasts lift it); send files ≤50 MB, download ≤20 MB; 429 'Too Many Requests' with retry_after. Telegram Business: a Business account owner can connect a bot (BusinessConnection, getBusinessConnection) and the bot acts in the OWNER's private chats via business_connection_id — official, consented, not an unofficial user-bot. Personal-account automation through MTProto clients is forbidden for us (registry / rules) — human lane.

sdks: Community libraries in every language (python-telegram-bot, telegraf, …) — the Bot API itself is plain HTTPS (core.telegram.org/bots/api)

endpoints.call: sendMessage {chat_id, text, parse_mode, message_thread_id, reply_parameters{message_id}, business_connection_id}

endpoints.purpose: group / forum admin (bot must be admin with the right)

reference.limits: - FAQ: ≤ 1 message / second per chat, ≤ 20 messages / minute in a group, ≈ 30 messages / second overall for bulk (paid broadcasts raise it); 429 with `retry_after`. - Bots cannot message a user who has not started them (no cold DM); bots never see other bots' messages; privacy mode hides non-command group messages unless disabled or the bot is admin. - Personal-account automation (MTProto clients, "user bots") is forbidden for this product — draft, human sends.

fields.name: token
fields.help: Bot token from @BotFather. It is part of the URL path: 'All queries to the Telegram Bot API must be served over HTTPS and need to be presented in this form: https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/METHOD_NAME' (https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#making-requests).

adapter.envelope_note: Every response is 'a JSON object, which always has a Boolean field ok' with `description`, `error_code` and `parameters` (retry_after) on failure (https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#making-requests). ok:false answers become isError results.
adapter.rate_note: Bot FAQ: 'avoid sending more than one message per second' in a chat, 'not more than 20 messages per minute' in a group, 'about 30 messages per second' overall; 429 with retry_after (https://core.telegram.org/bots/faq). One client-side bucket at 1/s.

me.note: getMe returns the bot's User object (id, is_bot, first_name, username).

send.note: `to` is the chat_id ('Unique identifier for the target chat or username of the target channel'). `subject` and `channel` are ignored. Bots cannot message a user who has not started them. message_id is an integer within the chat (the sent Message is under raw).

list_inbound.note: Long-polling queue, not a paged inbox: getUpdates returns the pending updates (kept up to 24 hours) and 'will not work if an outgoing webhook is set up'. This tool never sends `offset`, so it does not confirm/consume updates and repeated calls return the same pending updates; `page` and `since` are ignored and next_page is not meaningful. Updates that are not messages have no text; chat and sender ids are integers under raw.message.chat.id / raw.message.from.id.

not_offered.reply: sendMessage replies through `reply_parameters` ({message_id, chat_id, ...}), a nested object the adapter's flat body map cannot express (the former reply_to_message_id parameter is no longer in the sendMessage table, https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendmessage).
not_offered.get_thread: The Bot API has no method that returns the messages of a chat or thread; inbound messages arrive only through getUpdates or a webhook (https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#getting-updates).
not_offered.mark_read: No read-marking method exists in the Bot API (https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#available-methods).
